title: Troop carrier fleets and air strength, June to August 1944
author: Tov Binyamin Brog

sources.title: L. F. Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I (1962)
W. F. Craven and J. L. Cate, The Army Air Forces in World War II, vol. III, Europe: Argument to V-E Day

pageNote: Page numbers come from the running heads of the OCR texts and may be one or two pages off.

transport.note: Allied air resources when the assault began: troop carriers and transports, RAF and associated 460, USAAF 900; over 3,500 gliders. Engine: sides[0].transport.aircraft = 1360
AEAF planning figure: 1,000 troop carriers and 120 transports. Kept as a cross-check; Ellis's 1,360 is the figure the engine uses

IX Troop Carrier Command had a surplus of C-47 and C-53 aircraft much of the time after D-Day and later reached up to 1,400 aircraft and 2,000 gliders. No figure for 1 September; the engine keeps the D-Day fleet

lifts.note: Final airborne plan of 31 May: drop from 0200, gliders at 0400
Final airborne plan of 31 May: landing from 0121, west of the 101st

Carried by 38 Group RAF (Albemarle: 295, 296, 297, 570 Sqns; Stirling: 190, 196, 299, 620 Sqns; Halifax: 298, 644 Sqns) and 46 Group RAF (Dakota: 48, 233, 271, 512, 575 Sqns). Aircraft numbers per lift to read from Ellis ch. VIII

airSupply.note: During the Channel storm that began on 19 June troop carriers brought in about 1,400 tons of critical supplies

airfieldBuild.note: Plan: two emergency landing strips on D-Day; two refuelling and rearming strips on Omaha by D+3; four advanced landing grounds on Omaha and one on Utah by D+8; five on Omaha and three on Utah by D+14
The Utah emergency strip at Hebert was finished at 2115 on D-Day; detachments for Omaha could not land until 7 June
By the end of August 23 airfields had been built or repaired for 83 and 84 Groups RAF
IX Engineer Command built or rehabilitated 241 airfields in the whole campaign

strength.note: Third Air Fleet; pairs are strength and serviceable. Engine: sides[1].transport.aircraft = 31
Only 319 aircraft were able to operate on D-Day
Reinforcements to Air Corps II by 10 June
About 1,000 aircraft of all types a week after D-Day; most new units arrived days or weeks late by rail to bombed fields

strength.event: bombers switch to minelaying and circling torpedoes against shipping
Air Corps X anti-shipping aircraft withdrawn to Norway and Germany early in July
strength.note: Ellis says early July; day chosen by Claude

strength.event: fuel restrictions: fighters free only against heavy bombers; reconnaissance and ground attack limited; four-engined bombers grounded
two fighter units sent from Germany; forward air forces move back toward the Belgian frontier

strength.note: Last week of August: about 420 fighters in Belgium and northeast France; bombers and night fighters back to Holland and northwest Germany
